works.title: Spatial and Machine Learning Analysis of District-Level Health Insurance Inequities in Ghana
works.synopsis: A district-level account of health-insurance exclusion across Ghana. Spatial clustering and decision-tree analysis are used to identify where uninsurance, poverty and literacy barriers intersect.

metrics.label: feature importance
metrics.note: Illiteracy in the reported decision tree

methods.name: District GIS
methods.role: Mapped insurance exclusion across all Ghana districts.

methods.name: Spatial autocorrelation
methods.role: Tested whether high and low values formed geographic clusters.

methods.name: Decision tree
methods.role: Ranked structural factors associated with high uninsurance.

methods.name: Priority framework
methods.role: Converted the analysis into a ten-district diagnostic Red List.

works.caveat: The article reports district-level ecological associations. The companion dataset below comes from a related reproducible NHIS pipeline and is presented as a portfolio artifact, not as a re-analysis of the published article.
works.citation: Ghanem, V. G. (2026). Spatial and Machine Learning Analysis of District-Level Health Insurance Inequities in Ghana. Cureus, 18(1), e101984. https://doi.org/10.7759/cureus.101984

works.title: HIV Prognosis in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Narrative Review of Mortality Trends, Structural Determinants, and Policy Implications
works.venue: International Journal of Medical and Health Research 3(2)
works.synopsis: A narrative synthesis of HIV mortality, prognosis and the structural conditions that shape outcomes across sub-Saharan Africa.

metrics.label: studies reviewed
metrics.note: Peer-reviewed evidence in the site record

methods.name: Narrative synthesis
methods.role: Integrated evidence across heterogeneous clinical and policy studies.

methods.name: Mortality trend review
methods.role: Tracked prognosis and mortality patterns across settings.

methods.name: Structural determinant mapping
methods.role: Grouped social, service and policy influences on outcomes.

methods.name: Policy interpretation
methods.role: Connected evidence gaps to health-system priorities.

works.caveat: This is a narrative review. The console presents its verified scope and themes; it does not convert the review into a synthetic statistical model.
works.citation: Ghanem, V. G. (2025). HIV Prognosis in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Narrative Review of Mortality Trends, Structural Determinants, and Policy Implications. International Journal of Medical and Health Research, 3(2). https://doi.org/10.61424/ijmhr.v3i2.346

works.title: Socio-Behavioral and Spatial Determinants of HIV/AIDS Incidence in Ghana: An Ecological Cross-Sectional Study with Explainable Machine Learning
works.synopsis: A regional panel study joining epidemiological, sociobehavioral and health-infrastructure signals with spatial clustering and explainable machine learning.

metrics.label: panel observations
metrics.note: Monthly records across the study frame

methods.name: Panel construction
methods.role: Joined incidence, ART, testing and structural indicators.

methods.name: Spatial clustering
methods.role: Identified regional concentration and residual patterns.

methods.name: Random Forest and XGBoost
methods.role: Modelled non-linear associations in the panel.

methods.name: SHAP and PDP
methods.role: Explained model behaviour and threshold patterns.

works.caveat: The study is ecological and region-level. Associations and model explanations do not establish individual-level or causal effects.
works.citation: Ghanem, V. G. (2025). Socio-Behavioral and Spatial Determinants of HIV/AIDS Incidence in Ghana: An Ecological Cross-Sectional Study with Explainable Machine Learning. Advances in Infectious Diseases, 15(4), 669-694. https://doi.org/10.4236/aid.2025.154050

works.title: Forecasting HIV/AIDS Incidence in Ghana: A Retrospective Observational Study Using Ensemble Machine Learning Models
works.synopsis: A forecasting study comparing ensemble and regression approaches for short-horizon HIV incidence projections in Ghana.

metrics.label: model families
metrics.note: RF, XGBoost, gradient boosting and voting

methods.name: Time-series preparation
methods.role: Structured incidence records for horizon-based evaluation.

methods.name: Ensemble modelling
methods.role: Compared complementary tree and voting estimators.

methods.name: Forecast diagnostics
methods.role: Tracked performance as the forecast horizon increased.

methods.name: Interactive delivery
methods.role: Published results through a Streamlit dashboard.

works.caveat: This is a preprint. Results should be interpreted as work under scholarly review, not as a validated public-health forecasting service.
works.citation: Ghanem, V. G. (2025). Forecasting HIV/AIDS Incidence in Ghana: A Retrospective Observational Study Using Ensemble Machine Learning Models [Preprint]. Research Square. https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-6639193/v1
